metadata.title: Annual Reportable Labeling Changes for New Drug Applications and Abbreviated New Drug Applications for Nonprescription Drug Products

metadata.legal_basis: FDA Guidance Document (21 CFR 10.115). Guidance states FDA's current thinking and is not binding unless a statute or regulation requires it; the official text governs.

candidates.statement: Certain nonprescription drug products that are new drugs within the meaning of section 201(p) of 46 the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act (FD&C Act) are subject to approval on the basis of an 47 NDA or ANDA submitted under sections 505(b) or 505(j) of the FD&C Act, respectively. A 48 “nonprescription drug” is a drug that is not subject to the requirements of section 503(b)(1) of the 49 FD&C Act. 3
candidates.context: FDA evaluates whether the data and information submitted as part of an NDA or ANDA for a 52 nonprescription drug product demonstrate that the drug product is safe and effective for 53 nonprescription use under the conditions prescribed, recommended, or suggested in its proposed 54 labeling. 4 A nonprescription drug must be labeled with adequate directions for use. 5 Adequate 55 directions for use are the directions under which the consumer (layman) can use the drug safely 56 and for the purposes for which it is intended. 6 Therefore, labeling for a nonprescription drug 57 product 7 enables consumers to appropriately self-select and use the nonprescription drug product 58 safely and effectively without the supervision of a health care practitioner. 59

candidates.statement: After FDA approves an NDA or ANDA, an applicant may make, or in certain cases propose to 67 FDA, changes to the approved application. Section 506A of the FD&C Act and FDA regulations 68 under 21 CFR §§ 314.70, 314.71, and 314.97 establish certain requirements for making and 69 reporting to FDA changes to an approved NDA or ANDA, including an NDA or ANDA for a 70 nonprescription drug product. The regulations address changes that must be approved by FDA 71 before distribution of a drug product made with such changes, as well as changes for which FDA 72 approval is not required before distribution and changes that must be submitted in annual reports. 73 Changes to an approved NDA or ANDA, including labeling changes, are categorized into one of 74 three reporting categories: major, moderate, or minor. 11
candidates.context: 10 Actual use studies provide information on how consumers will use the drug product once purchased. candidates.context: B. Additional Considerations for Minor Labeling Changes 217 • Generally, changes to the content in the DFL of an approved nonprescription drug 221 product are not considered minor changes and may not be documented in an annual 222 report. 27 However, certain changes to the DFL may be considered minor, including 223 changing color of DFL and moving the tamper-evident statement from the DFL to the 224 outer carton (see section III.A. of this guidance for examples). 225
